question: A bucket has 60 litres of a solution with sugar and water in the ratio 5:1. If 12 litres of the solution are replaced with water, what is the new ratio?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining solution after removing 12 litres = 60 − 12 = 48 litres.

Quantity of Sugar in 48 litres = 48 × (5/6) = 40 litres.

Quantity of Water in 48 litres = 48 × (1/6) = 8 litres.

After adding 12 litres of water, new water quantity = 8 + 12 = 20 litres.

New ratio of Sugar to Water = 40 : 20 = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total volume of solution = 60 litres

Initial ratio of Sugar to Water = 5 : 1

Volume of mixture replaced with water = 12 litres

**Formula Used:**

Quantity of component = (Ratio of component ÷ Total Ratio parts) × Total Quantity

 Replacement Process
 
 
 
 
• 
 
 Sugar: 40 L
 Water: 8 L
 Remaining 48L

 +

 
 
 Water: 12 L
 Added 12L

 =

 
 
 
• 
 
 Sugar: 40 L
 Water: 20 L
 Final 60L

⇒ Amount of mixture remaining after removal = 60 − 12 = 48 litres

⇒ The ratio of Sugar to Water in the remaining mixture remains exactly 5 : 1

⇒ Total ratio parts = 5 + 1 = 6 parts

⇒ Amount of Sugar in remaining mixture = (5 ÷ 6) × 48 = 40 litres

⇒ Amount of Water in remaining mixture = (1 ÷ 6) × 48 = 8 litres

⇒ Now, 12 litres of pure water is added to the mixture.

⇒ Total Water in the new mixture = 8 + 12 = 20 litres

⇒ Total Sugar in the new mixture remains 40 litres

⇒ New ratio of Sugar to Water = 40 : 20 = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Replacement Principle

When a part of a uniformly mixed solution is removed, the concentration or ratio of the components in the remaining mixture stays exactly the same as the original mixture.

Rule of Alligation

Used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given concentrations/prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired concentration: Ratio = (C₂ − Cₘ) ÷ (Cₘ − C₁).

Successive Replacement Formula

If an initial volume V of pure liquid is repeatedly replaced by x volume of water 'n' times, the final volume of pure liquid left in the container = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.
